NE-2025-LR385.title: Interim study to examine any issues within the jurisdiction of the Government, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee of the Legislature that may arise in the interim

actions.text: Referred to Government, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee

NE-2025-LR385.aiSummary: Would direct the Government, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee to do an interim study of any issues that come up within its area of work. After the study, the committee would report its findings and recommendations to the Legislature or the Legislative Council.

NE-2025-LR441.title: Interim study relating to the applicability for residential versus commercial building codes and the implications of enacting LB1227, introduced in the One Hundred Ninth Legislature, Second Session
NE-2025-LR441.aiSummary: A legislative resolution would direct the Urban Affairs Committee to study how residential and commercial building codes apply and what could happen if LB1227 is enacted. The study would work with the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment to review energy impact studies and look at the return on investment for residential codes. It would also seek a source to explain the return on investment for commercial codes.

NE-2025-LR434.title: Interim study to examine how the existing learning community as defined in section 79-2101 interacts with and impacts the city of the metropolitan class in which it exists
NE-2025-LR434.aiSummary: The resolution would direct the Urban Affairs Committee to study how the existing learning community works with and affects the metropolitan class city where it is located. The study would look at rules, funding, student results, special education, and how money is shared among districts and programs. It would also look at work with school districts, cities, and other local groups, and then report findings and recommendations to lawmakers.

NE-2025-LR476.title: Interim study to examine the fiscal, constitutional, and administrative implications of adopting LB1095, 2026, relating to divesting assets of the retirement systems from the People's Republic of China

actions.text: Referred to Nebraska Retirement Systems Committee

NE-2025-LR476.aiSummary: The Nebraska Legislature would direct the Nebraska Retirement Systems Committee to do an interim study on LB1095, a proposed law about moving retirement system assets out of investments tied to the People’s Republic of China. The study would look at fiscal, constitutional, and administrative issues, including costs, long-term revenue effects, and how the plan could be carried out. After the study, the committee would report its findings and recommendations to the Legislature or the Legislative Council.

NE-2025-LR448.title: Interim study to review the quality and availability of assistance to Nebraska veterans and their families

actions.text: Referred to Government, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee

NE-2025-LR448.aiSummary: This resolution would direct a legislative committee to study the quality and availability of help for Nebraska veterans and their families. The study would look at veteran service officers, the benefits they help with, federal rules for their accreditation, related penalties, how veterans learn what benefits they may get, and the veterans disability claims review process. The committee would report its findings and recommendations to the Legislature or Legislative Council.

NE-2025-LB985.aiSummary: Nebraska lawmakers changed rules for guardians and conservators, which are people or companies appointed to help manage someone’s personal or money matters. The changes cover court appointments, removal or resignation, and the powers and duties of guardians and conservators. The bill also gives some people the right to attend certain court hearings and lets courts award costs and expenses in these cases.

NE-2025-LB894.aiSummary: The bill changes rules for the Grain Dealer Act and the Grain Warehouse Act. It would send investment earnings in the Grain Dealer and Grain Warehouse Cash Fund back into that fund, and keep that money from being moved to the General Fund or another state fund. It also states that license fee revenue should not be more than 25% of the commission’s costs to carry out these laws.

NE-2025-LB803.aiSummary: Approved by the governor, this law creates a first-time home buyer savings account program and changes several tax and property tax rules in Nebraska. It also changes parts of the sports arena financing law, the property tax growth limit law, homestead exemptions, and income taxes. votes.motion: Advanced to Enrollment and Review Initial

NE-2025-LB215.aiSummary: The bill would require Nebraska agencies to set up a program for second chance relief for some committed offenders, including people serving long or life sentences. It would let eligible people be reviewed for a sentence commutation, or reduction, after serving 25 years if the offense happened before age 26, or 30 years if it happened at age 26 or older. The process would involve the Department, the Division of Parole Supervision, the Board of Parole, and the Board of Pardons.

NE-2025-LB1124.aiSummary: The bill would raise the state tax on several tobacco and nicotine products, including snuff, electronic nicotine delivery systems, alternative nicotine products, and other tobacco products. It would also change how the tax is figured and say who must pay it in some sales. The money collected would still be used and split under a state law on cigarette tax proceeds, and the act would become operative on July 1, 2026.

NE-2025-LB1096.aiSummary: The measure was approved by the governor and would add new rules for some consultants working for a Chinese military company in Nebraska. Before they start influencing state policy, they would have to file detailed information and say they are acting for a foreign adversary of the United States. It would also let some public records be kept private and set civil fines of $100,000 per violation, with higher fines for repeat violations.
